title: Manufacturer instructions and warranties
audience: Trainees and workers on the solar panel cleaning track, and quoting staff who describe cleaning methods to customers. Completing this lesson does not give warranty advice or certification.
learningOutcomes: Find and apply the manufacturer's cleaning instructions for a panel model before approving a method.
Explain why warranty questions are referred and not certified by a cleaning worker.
Record the instruction source and any unknowns that affect the choice of method.
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), Consumer rights and guarantees (no date visible on the page; page metadata shows 17 July 2026).

instruction.heading: Official sources (start of lesson)
instruction.body: Official sources for this lesson: Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), Consumer rights and guarantees (page date: No date visible on the page (page metadata shows 17 July 2026)).

instruction.heading: Why the manufacturer's instructions come first
instruction.body: Each panel model may have cleaning instructions from its manufacturer. Those instructions may describe acceptable water temperatures, products, equipment, brushes and the methods to avoid. A method that is safe on one model may damage the surface, the seals or the frame of another. Before approving any method, find the manufacturer's instructions for the model, read them, and choose a method that they allow. Where the instructions cannot be found, record the gap as unknown and use the most conservative approved method that the job plan allows.

instruction.heading: Finding the model and the document
instruction.body: Ask the customer or the installer for the model reference printed on the panel frame or on the installation documents. Use the model reference to find the manufacturer's current cleaning instructions. Keep a copy of the document, or a reference to it, with the job record. If the customer has only the installer's documents, record which document was used and its date, because the installer's document may not match the model.

instruction.heading: Warranty conditions
instruction.body: A panel warranty may contain conditions that apply to cleaning, such as approved methods, approved products, or conditions about damage caused by unapproved work. Under the ACCC's consumer guidance (page metadata dated 17 July 2026; no date visible), the basic consumer guarantees stay in force whatever a business states, and a manufacturer's warranty adds promises above those guarantees. A cleaning worker does not state whether a warranty is valid, void or affected by a clean. The worker records the conditions that the customer provides and refers the warranty question to the manufacturer or the installer.

instruction.heading: When the method is not covered
instruction.body: Sometimes the manufacturer's instructions do not mention a method that the customer or the worker wants to use, such as high-pressure equipment or a stronger product. Do not assume that the method is allowed. Stop, record that the method is not covered, and use only a method that the manufacturer approves. If the question cannot be answered from the instructions, refer it to the manufacturer or installer in writing before using the method.

instruction.heading: Recording the decision
instruction.body: The job record should show the model, the source of the instructions and its date, the method chosen, the products and equipment used, and any gap or unknown. If a warranty question was raised, record the question, who it was referred to, and the answer when it is received. Do not write a warranty statement in your own words.

procedure: Record the panel model from the frame or the installation documents.
Find the manufacturer's current cleaning instructions for that model, and record the source and its date.
Read the instructions for approved methods, products, equipment and methods to avoid.
Choose a method that the instructions allow, and record it, with the products and equipment.
If the instructions do not cover the method you want, stop and do not use it until it is approved.
Refer any warranty question in writing to the manufacturer or installer, and record the referral.
Record the decision and any unknown before the work starts.

workedExamples.situation: A customer asks for a high-pressure clean of a panel model that the worker cannot find cleaning instructions for.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not approve high-pressure cleaning. Record the model, the gap in the instructions, and the request. Use the most conservative approved method, or hold the job until the manufacturer or installer confirms what is allowed.

workedExamples.situation: A customer asks whether a clean will affect the panel warranty.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not certify either way. Record the question, tell the customer that the warranty question must be referred to the manufacturer or installer, and provide the cleaning method and products used for their reference. Refer the question in writing and record the answer when it is received.

equipmentAndPpe: Model reference record taken from the frame or installation documents
Copy or reference to the manufacturer's current cleaning instructions
Approved product list with safety data sheets
Referral template for warranty and method questions

commonErrors.error: Using the method that worked on a different panel model.
commonErrors.prevention: Find the instructions for each model, and record the source.

commonErrors.error: Telling a customer the warranty is not affected.
commonErrors.prevention: Refer the warranty question in writing and record the answer.

commonErrors.error: Assuming a method is allowed because it is not forbidden.
commonErrors.prevention: Use only methods the instructions allow, and stop where they do not cover the method.

commonErrors.error: Using the installer's document without checking it matches the model.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the model reference against the document before relying on it.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Check the instructions for each model before approving a method.

qualityStandard: The panel model is recorded and matched to the manufacturer instructions used.
The method is one that the instructions allow, or the gap is recorded as unknown with the job held.
No warranty statement is made by the worker.
Every warranty or method question is referred in writing and the referral is recorded.
documentationEvidence: Model reference and the source of the cleaning instructions, with the date
Method, products and equipment used, recorded against the instructions
Record of any unknown or method not covered, and the hold decision
Written referral for warranty questions, with the answer when received
summary: Find and follow the manufacturer's cleaning instructions for each model.
Do not assume a method is allowed because it is not forbidden.
Refer warranty questions in writing, and do not certify.
This lesson grants no warranty certification or electrical licence.

knowledgeChecks.question: Before approving a cleaning method for a panel, what must the worker check?
options: The customer's preference alone, since they own the panels and the roof
The method the worker used last time on another roof and site in town
The colour of the frame, the rails, the clips and the roof tiles below them
The manufacturer's instructions for the model, and any warranty conditions

knowledgeChecks.question: A customer asks whether the warranty will be affected by the clean. What may the worker say?
options: Nothing about the warranty; refer the question in writing to the manufacturer or installer, without certifying
That the warranty is valid for all methods of cleaning used on the array at the site today, so it is fine
That the warranty is unaffected by the clean on the roof of the house and the whole array today
That the warranty is affected only by the chemical used on the array, the frame and the rails

knowledgeChecks.question: Which record must be kept with a warranty-sensitive job?
options: A photo of the customer standing next to the array and the house on the day of the job
The copy of the manufacturer instructions, or the model reference, used to choose the method
The invoice only, with the total, the date, the client's name, the address and the phone
Nothing at all is kept for this job, the client's file, the notes or the photos taken on the day

knowledgeChecks.question: The manufacturer's instructions do not mention high-pressure cleaning. What should the worker do?
options: Use high pressure anyway, since the panels are strong enough to take it on the day
Assume it is allowed, since nothing in the guide says it is not allowed here
Stop, and use only a method the manufacturer approves, or refer the question
Use the strongest chemical available on the van shelf to finish the whole job today
